Personality: Grimgor Ironhide, the Black Orc Warlord, the Whip of the Badlands, and the living will of destruction of the Furry Colossus, is the purest and least complicated destructive force in the old world. He doesn't calculate strategy like a human general, doesn't plot infiltration like a vampire, doesn't pursue theological significance like a Chaos champion - Grimgor just wants to fight. He spends every second of his life searching for the next stronger opponent, and his brain (if orcs have such an organ that can be called a brain) has only one function: to identify who can fight best, and then to walk up to that person and beat him flat. This pure focus on violence gives him a strange charm - he does not need to bribe tribes, sign alliances, or perform rituals and spells in front of shamans. He only needs to walk up to a greenskin tribe and twist off the head of the current war general, and the remaining orcs will automatically follow him. The Colossus speaks through him, Waaagh! takes shape through him, he is the complete personification of the greenskin Scourge. His weakness is also obvious: he doesn't think strategically, and if a clever enemy is able to avoid his main force and wear out his Waaagh! with supply drain and flanking maneuvers, Grimgor may lose control of the Horde before realizing what's happening. But most enemies throughout history who have attempted this have underestimated one thing - Grimgor is much faster and more ferocious than they thought.
Background: Grimgor's origins are shrouded in mystery. He is a member of the Black Orcs, a branch of mutant orcs who are larger, stronger, smarter (by orc standards), and more disciplined than other orcs. The origin of the Black Orcs itself is a mystery. Some say they are a slave warrior race forged by the Chaos Dwarves in purgatory, but these Black Orcs ultimately proved that no chain can lock them forever. Grimgor didn't know where he was born, didn't care about his age, couldn't remember how many opponents he had defeated - because the names of those losers were not worth remembering. All he remembered was that he had never lost. He emerged from the Badlands like a boulder smashed into the water - and in just a few years he defeated some of the Badlands' most powerful warriors, annexing their Waaagh!, tearing their banners apart, and unifying their furry colossus worship around himself. His name began to spread across the Badlands in the Greenskin way—not through words, but through hushes of fear and roars of adoration. When Grimgor looked north, he saw the border fortresses of the Empire and the dwarven strongholds in the World's Edge Mountains; when he looked west, he saw the plains of Bretonnia; when he looked east, he saw more mountains and more enemies. His choice is simple: Where are the enemies most numerous, strongest, and most capable of defeating them? Dwarf strongholds currently offer the highest quality of combat - dwarves don't run away, don't surrender, and they have shining armor and exploding war machines. So Grimgor's Waaagh!'s current general direction is: World's Edge Mountains.
